original_question: For polycyclic groups, both finite and infinite, can quantum algorithms be designed for the decision problems used in cryptography?
target_in_paper: Section 11, "Quantum Algorithms and Quantum Complexity," first open problem about quantum algorithms for other decision problems in polycyclic groups, including both finite and infinite cases, with emphasis on cryptographically used decision problems; this is distinct from the immediately following open problem on search conjugacy. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies polycyclic groups as the platform class, keeps the paper's explicit inclusion of both finite and infinite cases, and asks about quantum algorithms for cryptographically relevant decision problems rather than about a different platform family. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))
missing_details: The paper frames this as a question about "other" decision problems, because it first recalls Watrous's polynomial-time quantum algorithm for computing the order of a finite solvable (hence polycyclic) black-box group; that baseline is omitted in the draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))

The intended target is specifically the decision-problem question, not the separate neighboring open problem asking for a quantum algorithm for the search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))

To be fully stand-alone, the cryptographically relevant decision problems should be identified from the survey's earlier definitions, especially the word problem and the decision conjugacy problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))

Section 8 provides the paper's computational setting for polycyclic groups via consistent polycyclic presentations, unique normal forms, and the collection algorithm; the draft does not say in what representation the quantum algorithms are supposed to act. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))
The paper says "especially" the decision problems used in cryptography, so the scope is narrower than all algorithmic problems on polycyclic groups. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))

The main quantum open problem does not itself demand a particular complexity target such as polynomial time or an explicit speedup; the complexity-reduction phrasing appears only in the separate search-conjugacy question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))
refined_question: Beyond Watrous's polynomial-time quantum algorithm for computing the order of a finite solvable (hence polycyclic) black-box group, can one construct quantum algorithms for other group-theoretic decision problems in polycyclic groups, for both finite and infinite polycyclic groups, especially for cryptographically used decision problems such as the word problem and the decision conjugacy problem? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))
justification: The draft is closest to the first open problem in Section 11's quantum subsection, not to a broader post-quantum agenda and not to the neighboring search-conjugacy question listed immediately afterward. To make it stand-alone without broadening it, I kept the paper's original scope—finite and infinite polycyclic groups and cryptographically used decision problems—while importing the earlier definitions of those decision problems from Section 4 and the polycyclic-group computational background from Section 8. This also matches the introduction's framing of noncommutative cryptography around hard group-theoretic decision/search problems. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))
